This is an independent unverified scoped reconstruction, with no incoming correctness grant and no supplied verdict used as a mathematical premise. The domain is K=C((s)), |s|=exp(-1/8), t=s^8, Y=(G_m²)^an_K and ACTUAL X=Y/<(t,2),(3,t)>. Original P16.7 is not claimed solved.

Geometry and nonalgebraization. Periods translate tau=(-log|z1|,-log|z2|) by Z². Ordinary boxes of widths less than one give injective quotient charts; the compact unit polyannulus covers X. Finitely many deck graphs meet bounded chart products. Conrad–Temkin4.2.3 glues local etale-relation quotients;4.2.4 descends the coherent diagonal ideal along a FINITE flat quasi-finite chart cover with finite fibres, never along the infinite-sheeted Y->X. X is compact, good, strict, smooth, separated, boundaryless, connected, pure dimension two and proper.

GrusonIV.5 Theorem1 gives SK^0=0 only for products of divisible-radius discs and unit circles. Determinants trivialize line bundles there. Filling a wide annulus by its inner disc and gluing along the inner circle with Tate–Kiehl coherent gluing (Van der Put2.14–2.16.3), inductively, gives Pic(P_m)=0 for P_m={|s|^m<=|zi|<=|s|^-m}. For a unit b=sum b_beta z^beta on P_m, its Gauss log norm is affine because it and its negative are convex. An interior maximizing monomial alpha agrees throughout the box, so |b_beta/b_alpha|exp((m/8)|beta-alpha|_1)<=1. Normalize consecutive frames by scalar monomials. Their transitions 1+g_m satisfy ||g_m||_(P_j)<=|s|^(m-j) for j<m. Products and inverse tails converge on each fixed P_j and produce a global frame. Thus Pic(Y)=0. Global units are scalar monomials, since another exponent would dominate on a tropical ray.

Multipliers c_i z^(h_i), h1=(A,B),h2=(C,D), obey t^C2^D=3^At^B. Hence C=B,A=D=0 and h1=(0,k),h2=(k,0). If k!=0, lambda=lambda1 lambda2^(sign k) has exponent h=(k sign k,k) with v(lambda^h)=2|k|>0. A section has recurrence a_(m+jh)=a_m c^j lambda^(-jm-hj(j+1)/2), whose negative quadratic valuation growth contradicts Laurent convergence. If k=0, at most one monomial occurs, and sections with identical multipliers are proportional. The pole ideal of meromorphic F is the coherent kernel of multiplication by its numerator modulo its denominator. Regular local factoriality (Stacks0AG0) and regular/flat analytic restrictions (Ducros2.1.3(2),(5),2.1.4) make it invertible and preserve this kernel. Its global frame on Y and its product with F have identical multipliers; therefore Gamma(X,M_X)=K. A finite-type algebraic-space algebraization would be smooth proper integral dimension two by Conrad–Temkin2.3.1. Stacks086U,0BB1,0EN6,0ENA,0END identify its rational/meromorphic field on a dense scheme locus, with the generic and weak-associate hypotheses supplied by smoothness. Flat analytic local maps and a closed point test inject that transcendence-degree-two field into K, contradiction. Nonalgebraizability is proved over this K, not asserted after every extension.

Positivity and bounded calculus. Locally rho=|tau|²/2, theta=DD rho; reference changes are affine unit logarithms. Saturated degree-one torus calibration gives theta² equal to twice Lebesgue measure on the reference Gauss section, raw M=2. Theta degenerates on residue bidiscs. C consists of continuous a whose rho+a belongs to the ENTIRE minimal continuous CLD psh sheaf8.1.7–8.1.8. CLD8.5.1,8.5.3,8.5.5–6,8.7.1–4,8.8.4–5 give actual positive symmetric products theta_a=theta+DDa, B(a,b)=theta_a wedge theta_b, MA(a)=B(a,a), gluing and mass two. Positive top currents and coefficients are Radon by7.2.8–12;15.7.1 supplies compatible tropical calculus on separated pure-dimensional analytic spaces. Arbitrary-multiplier closedness8.6.7 is not used.

All-stage Green is reconstructed using a positive Hilbert completion for each positive closed current T. Smooth gradients with strong limits and uniformly approximated functions form a sheaf, patched by partitions and Leibniz. A uniformly zero sequence with a strong gradient limit pairs to zero with every smooth test by closedness, so its gradient limit is zero. For L_Tf=DD(fT) signed Radon, Q_T(f,g)=-integral f L_Tg=-integral g L_Tf and Q_(T,chi)(f)=1/2 integral f² DDchi wedge T-integral chi f L_Tf. For uniformly convergent psh f_j, nested cutoffs chi,eta with eta=1 near supp chi and |f_j|<=B on the WHOLE supp eta give, with epsilon=||f_j-f_k|| there,
0<=Q_(T,chi)(f_j-f_k)<=epsilon²||DDchi wedge T||_TV/2+2B epsilon||chi||infinity||DDeta wedge T||_TV.
Strong gradients pass uniform limits, and minimality includes every continuous stage. This proves symmetric Green and Q_T(f)>=0 for continuous dpsh functions without arbitrary-current pullback.

E(a)=1/3 integral a[theta²+B(a,0)+MA(a)] is cubic. Green gives E'(a_t)=integral(b-a)MA(a_t), E''(a_t)=-2Q_(theta_at)(b-a)<=0. E is monotone and concave, E(0)=0, E(a+c)=E(a)+2c, and
E(b)-E(a)=1/3 integral(b-a)[MA(a)+B(a,b)+MA(b)].
For a<=b, each positive integral on the right is at most3(E(b)-E(a)).

Canonical generated calculus. G consists of ACTUAL presentations a_j in C decreasing pointwise to u with finite lower E. These are USC representatives including poles. Compact strict domination holds even for USC nets: if f_i decrease to f<h everywhere with h finite continuous, the increasing opens {f_i<h} cover compact X; finite subcover and directedness give one global late index. On finite simplices energies have degree at most three. Values at a finite unisolvent set converge, hence coefficients converge. For bounded v in C, P_j(t)=E((1-t)a_j+tv), R_j(t)=E(ta_j) give integral v MA(a_j)=P'_j(0)+R'_j(1), canonically. Span C is a uniformly dense vector lattice: small periodic smooth perturbations separate tropical classes, and globally capped Laurent-polynomial logarithms separate seminorms in one fibre, with zero collars and zero branches near zeros. The lattice identity is max(A(p-q),A(r-s))=2A max((p+s)/2,(r+q)/2)-A(q+s). Positive common mass and density give convergence against EVERY continuous test; compact-Hausdorff Riesz gives actual Radon MA(u), and polarization gives actual mixed products.

For u<=0, sequence monotone convergence gives integral(-u)mu<=D(mu)-E(u), integrability and presentation L1 convergence. Bounded tangent gives D(MA(a))=E(a)-integral a MA(a). Thus D_u=integral u MA(u) and D(MA(u))=E(u)-integral u MA(u). The formal polynomial coefficient partial_s E(tu+sv) at(1,0) equals integral v MA(u), first for bounded v, then by its decreasing presentation, coefficient convergence and integrability. This proves ALL FOUR moving moments for ANY presentations of u,v. Generated first variation follows. Clamps u^A=max(u,-A) satisfy 1_(u>-A)MA(u^A)=1_(u>-A)MA(u), excluding the ENTIRE contact set. For E(u)>=-C, discarded mass is <=3C/A. No discontinuous clamp is silently a continuous CLD product.

All bounded tests. For a,b,w<=0 of E>=-C, cocycle and tangent give integral(-p)MA(q)<=3C and integral(-p)B(q,r)<=6C. With f=a-b,g=(a+b)/2,h=w-g,

The transgression has signed value -integral f DDf wedge DDh. Since |h|<=-w+(-a-b)/2, each h-slot is bounded by12C+3C+6C=21C. Direct-sum Cauchy–Schwarz gives Q_theta_w(a-b)<=I/2+sqrt(42CI). For equal generated MA, ALL FOUR moving moments give I_j->0 for ANY presentations. Every FIXED bounded test gradient energy therefore tends to zero, without a common supnorm lower bound.

Actual point atoms without scalar extension. At total graded-dimension-two x, support kernel is zero by Abhyankar. Completion of K(z1,z2) adds no initials; Laurent-polynomial initials generate the graded field by fractions. Select two homogeneous independent initials represented by P1,P2. Their actual image is the weighted Gauss point of arbitrary positive real radii r_i=|Pi(x)|. CLD11.6.5(c) applies at relative interior, reduced target, dimensions<=2 and image graded dimension2.11.6.3 gives a compact local finite-flat rankD>0 representative with SINGLE Gauss fibre{x}. Pleasant-moment calibration14.5.2–3 gives degreeD upstairs. For psi=max(0,log(|P1|/r1),log(|P2|/r2)), the smooth log-sum-exp gradient fills the standard simplex of area1/2; raw2! gives mass1 concentrating at the vertex. Properness and singleton fibre give convergence against every actual continuous upstairs test to D delta_x. A global cap max(rho_a,delta+epsilon psi)-rho_a, zero on a collar, belongs to C through capped smooth logarithms and soft maxima. Its inner curvature is epsilon DDpsi, so MA(w_x)>=alpha_x delta_x, alpha_x=epsilon²D>0. The WHOLE bounded MA(w_x) has finite FULL dual. Consequently -u(x)<=(D(MA(w_x))+C)/alpha_x for u<=0,E(u)>=-C. For Laurent P(z2), CLD18.6.1–2 at boundaryless separated equidimensional hypotheses identifies T=DD max(0,log(|P|/rP)) with ACTUAL integration over P^-1(Gauss_rP). This new scoped theorem uses the independently reconstructed calculus, point atoms and all-Shilov determination of earlier own note n1. No supplied note is a premise. K,X,theta,C,G,E,MA,B and full dual are exactly those of n1: genuine nonalgebraizable X, raw mass2, all continuous stages, actual pointwise sequence-generated weights and no support restriction.

Quantitative theorem. For nonpositive a,b,w in C with a<=b and energies>=-C, C>=0, put delta=E(b)-E(a). Then
0<=integral(b-a)MA(w)<=F_C(delta),
F_C(d)=3d+sqrt(12C*(9d/2+sqrt(126Cd))).
F_C(d)->0 as d->0 without a common supnorm lower bound. At an actual MA(w) atom of size alpha, 0<=b(x)-a(x)<=F_C(delta)/alpha.

Proof. Let f=b-a>=0. The positive cocycle gives integral f MA(a)<=3delta. Green gives I(a,b)=Q_theta_a(f)+Q_theta_b(f)>=0, while positivity gives I<=integral f MA(a)<=3delta. Set T=theta_w+theta_a,k=w-a. Symmetric products give MA(w)-MA(a)=DD(kT). Therefore
integral f MA(w)=integral f MA(a)-Q_T(f,k)
<=3delta+sqrt(Q_T(f)Q_T(k)).
The all-test bound and Q_theta_a(f)<=I give Q_T(f)<=3I/2+sqrt(42CI). Also Q_T(k)=I(a,w)<=integral|a-w|(MA(a)+MA(w))<=12C, by |a-w|<=-a-w and four3C moment bounds. Substituting I<=3delta proves the formula. All multipliers here are bounded continuous dpsh and T is positive closed. The point bound uses positivity of the whole actual measure; it says nothing about finite full dual of a normalized Dirac component.

Generated ordered extension. Suppose u<=v in G, u,v<=B and energies>=L. Take arbitrary presentations A_j↓u,B_j↓v and replace B_j by max(A_j,B_j). This decreases in C to exactly v and dominates A_j. Compact strict domination discards initial terms so both<=B+1. Subtract B+1 from both and independently sup(w) from the fixed test. The single constant C>=max(0,2(B+1)-L,-E(w-sup(w))) works for every term. Energy differences tend to E(v)-E(u); finite full dual of MA(w) gives actual L1 convergence. Thus the integral bound passes to u,v. Full-dimensional endpoint values are finite by n1, so the point estimate passes too. Ordered u<=v with equal energy have identical full2 values; all-Shilov reconstruction gives u=v pointwise including poles.

Countable representation lemma, reconstructed without a supplied grant. Suppose u_k in G decrease with L=inf E(u_k)>-infinity. Choose presentations f_(k,j), enumerate ALL pairs as h_m, and set u=inf_k u_k=inf_m h_m. Put epsilon_n=2^-n,r_n=sum_(ell>n)epsilon_ell=2^-n. Compact strict domination selects k_n>=max(n,k_(n-1)) with u_(k_n)<h_m+epsilon_n for m<=n. For n>1 it also lies below v_(n-1)+epsilon_n. Choose a late presentation term v_n=f_(k_n,j_n) below all these finitely many continuous bounds. Their minimum is only a comparison bound and is NEVER inserted into the psh class. Then a_n=v_n+r_n decreases because epsilon_n+r_n-r_(n-1)=0. It dominates u and eventually lies below every h_m+epsilon_n+r_n. Its exact pointwise limit is u, including poles. E(a_n)>=E(u_(k_n))>=L, so u belongs to G. Order gives E(u)<=L; compact strict domination against a presentation of u plus epsilon gives L<=E(u). Therefore E(u_k)↓E(u).

ARBITRARY decreasing-net closure. Let u_i decrease in G over ANY directed I, with L=inf_iE(u_i)>-infinity. Restrict to a tail i>=i0; its pointwise and energy infima are unchanged by directedness. The tail has a common finite upper bound B from u_i0. Recursively choose i_n>=i_(n-1) with E(u_i_n)<=L+2^-n, by choosing an energy-near-infimum index and a directed upper bound. Countable closure gives v=inf_nu_i_n in G with E(v)=L. This sequence is NOT asserted cofinal in I.

Fix any tail index i and any full2 point x. Choose j_n>=i,i_n. Then u_j_n<=u_i_n,u_i and 0<=E(u_i_n)-E(u_j_n)<=2^-n. The ordered atom bound uses a single C_x depending only on B,L,w_x, independent of i,n,j_n, giving
0<=u_i_n(x)-u_j_n(x)<=F_(C_x)(2^-n)/alpha_x ->0.
All point values are finite. Thus v(x)<=u_i(x) for every i, while u=inf_i u_i<=v. Hence u=v at ALL full2 points without countable cofinality or countable tests.

The actual u is USC, since an infimum of USC functions is USC. GR Proposition4.2(4) makes rho+u classical psh by decreasing-NET closure. Rho+v is classical as generated. Every affinoid Shilov point is full2. The formula q(x)=inf_A max_GammaA q therefore gives u=v at EVERY point, including poles. Consequently the arbitrary net infimum belongs to the SAME original SEQUENCE-generated G, and E(u_i)↓E(u)=L. This constructs an actual analytic representative, not an abstract functional or coordinate-product representative.

Directed operator continuity. For finitely many decreasing energy-bounded nets, use their common directed product index. Every fixed convex combination decreases with a finite lower energy bound by concavity. The theorem supplies its actual generated limit and energy continuity. Values at a finite unisolvent cubic interpolation set converge, hence coefficients converge. The actual first-variation identities of n1 give MA convergence against C, ALL FOUR moving MA moments and mixed polarizations. Uniform density of span C and common mass2 give convergence against EVERY continuous analytic-space test. Thus integral u_i MA(v_i)->integral u MA(v), together with the self/cross moments. Fixed-u moving tests follow by using u as a constant net.

Arbitrary-support finite-full-dual net L1 continuity. Let mu be positive Radon, mass2, D(mu)<infinity. Choose a continuous sequence presentation a_m↓u, which converges in L1(mu) by n1. For fixed m and epsilon>0, compact strict domination against a_m+epsilon gives eventually u<=u_i<a_m+epsilon everywhere. Hence
0<=integral(u_i-u)mu<=integral(a_m-u)mu+2epsilon.
Choose m, then epsilon, then a sufficiently late index. This proves integral|u_i-u|mu->0. The set{u=-infinity} is a common mu-null set by full dual; outside it all u_i>=u are finite. No uncountable union of null sets is assumed. General measurable-net monotone convergence would be false: indicators of [0,1] minus a finite subset, directed by inclusion of finite subsets, decrease to0 while each Lebesgue integral is1. Our continuous-majorant argument avoids this error. That diagnostic is not a psh counterexample.

Downward filtered generated families are also covered by indexing their order. Real energy selects the same actual infimum without selecting a cofinal index subset. This removes the arbitrary-decreasing-net representation gate. It does not compactify NONORDERED sublevels: minima and inf-tail functions are not known psh/generated, so a rooftop/envelope input remains missing. Nor does it recognize a sufficient intrinsic E1 domain, prove obstacle orthogonality, construct a variational maximizer or solve every prescribed arbitrary-support finite-full-dual measure. Eligibility is not replaced by mu=MA(u).
